claim: The global tables best-practices page, which is documentation for version 2017.11.29 (Legacy) of global tables, says DynamoDB auto scaling is the recommended way to manage throughput capacity settings for replica tables that use provisioned mode, and that you can use on-demand mode if auto scaling does not satisfy your capacity changes (unpredictable workload) or you do not want to configure its settings.

qualifiers.condition: the page is for version 2017.11.29 (Legacy) of global tables

evidence.quote: This documentation is for version 2017.11.29 (Legacy) of global tables, which should be avoided for new global tables.
Using DynamoDB auto scaling is the recommended way to manage throughput capacity settings for replica tables that use the provisioned mode.

If auto scaling doesn't satisfy your application's capacity changes (unpredictable workload), or if you don't want to configure its settings (target settings for minimum, maximum, or utilization threshold), you can use on-demand mode to manage capacity for your global tables.
